correctness.rationale: The published dimension theorem makes the affine hull exactly the intersection of the zero-coordinate-sum hyperplane and the rank hyperplane. Orthogonal projection of the origin onto that affine hull gives \(c=-r/S\); every arrow root has norm squared \(2\) and rank scalar product \(-1\), yielding the exact common squared radius \(2-1/S\). The sphere is minimum enclosing exactly when its center lies in the vertex hull. Barycentric membership is equivalent to a nonnegative flow with divergence \(c\), and max-flow/min-cut converts this to the lower-ideal centered-rank inequalities. Failure of an ideal inequality gives strict separation and hence a strictly smaller enclosing sphere after a small center shift.

value.rationale: Directed edge polytopes are a canonical type-A root configuration with recent complete face theory. For rank-function quivers, the theorem extracts an exact Euclidean invariant from the combinatorial rank data: the entire vertex set lies on a sphere controlled by rank variance. The lower-ideal criterion then cleanly separates when this canonical sphere is genuinely the minimum enclosing sphere, linking convex geometry to feasible transshipment on the graded quiver. The criterion is nonvacuous and fails for natural connected graded quivers, so the result is not merely the observation that all root vectors have equal norm.
